prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the identification of its active form, which made possible incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single prize part for B042 naming Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. After the full first-round exchange I still find the scientific case the strongest on the shortlist, and I hold it on the substance and not on the six first places. The discovery is a physiological one: a proglucagon-derived hormone whose active GLP-1(7-36) form acts on islets, stomach and central satiety circuits. It was followed by receptor biology and by long-acting agonists that independent randomized outcome trials have tested over many years. Maturity is not in question. The citation I propose keeps the prize on the physiology and the active peptide and mentions the therapies only as a consequence, so that it does not assert a priority the committee cannot adjudicate and does not read as an award for a drug class. I do not favour a second part. Every second part I can examine carries an attribution gap at least as large as the one in B042, and a second part would push the GLP-1 credit below three names.
statement.case_against: The attribution is still the weak point, and the first-round discussion has not removed it. Mojsov's priority for the active peptide against Habener's group rests on my recollection, not on checked primary sources, and Habener is outside the credited names. Knudsen is excluded by the three-name cap although her engineering of long-acting agonists was not routine and made the discovery usable. A physiology-focused citation will be read by some as a slight to that step. If the committee cannot support Mojsov's claim for the active form, I would move Knudsen into the third place and reword the citation around the therapy as well as the hormone. I would not leave that place to a weaker basic claim and I would not keep the original wording unchanged. Long-term durability of weight loss and safety are still accumulating, though they do not affect the physiology.

responses.point: The chair asks how the tool-versus-discovery question should be settled for B029 and B004 so that it is applied the same way to both, and would keep the B042 citation on physiology so as not to assert a priority that cannot be adjudicated.
responses.response: I accept the request for consistency and propose one test for both. First, does the work rest on the discovery of a natural mechanism, and second, has it given new knowledge about physiology or disease that others could not have obtained otherwise? B029 passes both: the light-gated channel is a natural mechanism and the method has produced causal knowledge of circuits. B004 passes the second but mainly as an engineered chemistry and instrument platform, which is why I did not rank it. The test therefore does not remove B029 on principle, and I do not say it does. B029 fails for a separate reason, which is that six credited names cannot become three without leaving out a person with a real claim. I also agree with the chair's wording on B042. The citation should name the physiology and the active form and should not decide a priority dispute in the text.

responses.point: Linnarsson has moved from a Knudsen-inclusive trio to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, but says he accepts it mainly as the most coherent set and would record that Knudsen's omission is a real cost.
responses.response: I agree with the record he proposes. The omission of Knudsen is a cost and the committee should say so openly, not describe the trio as the only fair set. I also agree with his point that engineering a peptide that is degraded within minutes was not routine. Where we still differ slightly is on the status of that work. I regard it as a major step but as development of an existing discovery, and the prize for physiology or medicine has generally honoured the discovery. We agree on the fallback, since he and I would both put Knudsen in the third place if Mojsov's claim for the active form cannot be supported.

responses.point: Perlmann asks me how I would resolve the credit among the six names in B029 if the tool framing is acceptable, and says B041 deserves another look as a possible second part of a two-part prize.
responses.response: I cannot resolve the six names in B029 fairly, and I said so in round 1. A Deisseroth, Hegemann and Nagel trio is defensible, but it leaves out Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck, and I would not put forward a configuration that I think is unfair to any of them. That is why B029 stays in my alternatives only, behind B038. On B041, I considered her suggestion of a second part. Feldmann and Maini are the cleanest pair on the list, but the originating discovery is narrower than the GLP-1 chain, since TNF was already known and the new step was its role in rheumatoid arthritis and the clinical proof. A pair would also force Drucker, Holst or Mojsov out of B042. I do not support that trade.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius says she would not let attribution uncertainty push B042 below B038 or B013, since their credit lists have comparable gaps (Eshhar for CAR-T, Zhou for HPV), and that a two-part prize would force the GLP-1 credit down to one or two names.
responses.response: I agree on both points and my own comparison supports them. The Eshhar gap in B038 is a conceptual priority claim that sits inside the discovery itself, and the Rosenberg credit mixes two achievements. The gap in B042 is a dispute about one step, the identification of the active peptide, and a fallback (Knudsen) exists if it fails. The B042 gap is therefore narrower, and I would say so in the committee record. I also agree that splitting the prize would damage the strongest case to make room for a weaker one. I would keep B038 first among alternatives, but I would still want the Eshhar and Rosenberg questions resolved before it could stand alone.

responses.point: Sandberg says a Deisseroth, Hegemann and Nagel configuration is defensible as a second choice for B029, and that B029 is a tool enabling discovery and not a discovery about physiology.
responses.response: I partly agree. I accept that it is a second-choice configuration that the committee could defend, and that is why B029 remains my second alternative. I do not fully accept the framing of a tool versus a discovery about physiology. Channelrhodopsin is a discovery about a natural light-gated channel, and the method has answered physiological questions about how circuits produce behaviour. My reservations are the credit among six names and the early stage of clinical translation, not the status of the work as a discovery. I declare again that this field is close to my own and have tried to weigh it with extra care, which is why I do not put it above B038 despite my regard for the science.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1 peptide over Habener's group can be supported. My account relies on recollection and has not been checked against primary sources, and the choice of the third name depends on it.

Whether the committee will accept a citation that names the physiology and the active form without crediting the drug engineering by Knudsen, and whether that wording avoids asserting a disputed priority.
Whether the Eshhar and Rosenberg questions in B038 can be settled well enough for it to stand alone in a later year or as an alternative now.
Whether the test I proposed for B029 and B004 would be accepted by the committee, since my own field is close to B029.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict bears on any shortlisted ballot. I disclose, as before, a 2009 co-authored paper with Thomas Perlmann and a 2019 co-authored review with Sten Grillner, neither involving any credited name on the shortlist. My work on motor circuits places B029 near my field. I treat that as a reason for care in weighing it, which is why I have kept it as an alternative and not as my preferred part, and not as a ground for recusal. No new disclosure arose in the first-round exchange.
